details.description: GLM-5.3-Flash is Z.ai's first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series, accepting image, video, text and file input and producing text output. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 320 billion total and 18 billion active parameters, using a hybrid sparse-and-linear attention design that Z.ai says cuts attention computation by about 3.0x and KV-cache size by about 4.4x compared with GLM-5.3. It supports a 1M-token context window, always-on reasoning with adjustable thinking effort, function calling, and native visual understanding aimed at coding, UI and frontend review, and document or chart analysis. Z.ai launched it August 25, 2026 as a faster sibling to GLM-5.3 that it says outperforms the prior-generation GLM-5.2 across most evaluations.
advantages: Scores 63.4 on DeepSWE v1.1, up from GLM-5.2's 46.2, per Z.ai's documentation.
Scores 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1.1, per Together AI's model listing.
Z.ai reports cutting attention computation by about 3.0x and KV cache by about 4.4x versus GLM-5.3.
Natively processes image, video, text and file input for tasks such as reviewing rendered UI output and analyzing charts, per Z.ai's documentation.
disadvantages: Reasoning is always on and cannot be disabled, per Z.ai's documentation.
use_cases: Vision-driven UI and frontend coding, including reviewing rendered results and iterating
Document, chart and financial analysis combining text and images

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (1,048,575) and max_output_tokens (128,000) match Z.ai's own docs (1M context / 128K output) and Together AI's listing exactly. An initial Hugging Face card summary returned a conflicting '300,000 token' context figure, but two independent maker/host pages (docs.z.ai and Together AI) agree with the catalog's 1M figure, so the 300K figure looks like an extraction error and was not used. Catalog's image+text-input/text-output modality matches Z.ai's description of native multimodal (image/video/text/file) input.
